tour.overview:
West of Bangkok, the delta of the Mae Klong river is a flat land of coconut palms, orchards and canals, where for centuries people travelled and traded by boat. Damnoen Saduak's canal was dug in the 1860s on the orders of King Rama IV to link the Mae Klong and Tha Chin rivers, and its floating market, with women in straw hats selling from wooden boats, has become one of the classic images of Thailand. Nearby, at Maeklong, a market was built on the railway line itself: eight times a day, the vendors pull back their awnings and baskets as a train inches through, and then lay everything out again.

This private trip shows both with a licensed guide and a car. You time the visit to the train at Maeklong, explore the floating market by paddle boat, see how coconut sugar is made on a family farm, and have lunch by the river at Amphawa, a canal town of wooden houses.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Bangkok
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver, paddle boat
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Maeklong railway market and the passing train.
• Damnoen Saduak floating market by paddle boat.
• A coconut-sugar farm.
• Amphawa.

WHY THIS WORKS
We leave early to reach the floating market before it fills with coach groups, and time Maeklong to the train schedule, which most group tours miss.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, photographers and food lovers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you want temples and history, choose our Grand Palace tour or Ayutthaya.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Damnoen Saduak is busy and commercial; we take a paddle boat rather than a motorboat and visit the quieter side canals. The train schedule at Maeklong changes occasionally, and the line is sometimes closed for maintenance.

days.name: Maeklong railway market, Damnoen Saduak floating market, a coconut-sugar farm and lunch in Amphawa
days.description:
What to expect: the markets and canal life of the Mae Klong delta, with a licensed guide, private car, paddle boat and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 6:30 and drive west, about an hour and a half, into the delta. At Damnoen Saduak you board a wooden paddle boat, rowed by a local, and glide along the main canal among boats piled with mangoes, rambutans, dragon fruit and pomelos, vendors cooking noodle soup on board and selling coconut ice cream in a coconut shell. Your guide helps you bargain and taste, and the boat turns into quieter side canals lined with houses on stilts, orchards and spirit houses.

On the way to Maeklong you stop at a family coconut-sugar farm, where the sap collected from the flowers of coconut palms is boiled in large woks until it caramelises into the palm sugar used in Thai sweets. At the Maeklong railway market, the 'umbrella-closing market', you walk along the track between stalls of fish, vegetables and spices. When the bell rings, the vendors pull back their awnings and baskets within seconds, the train creeps through a few centimetres from the goods, and the market closes up behind it as if nothing happened. We time your visit to the train.

Lunch is in Amphawa, a canal town of wooden shophouses, at a restaurant by the water – grilled river prawns, fish cakes and a curry. In the early afternoon your driver takes you back to Bangkok, arriving at about 14:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
06:30 – Pick-up at your hotel in Bangkok.
08:00 – Damnoen Saduak floating market by paddle boat.
09:30 – Coconut-sugar farm.
10:30 – Maeklong railway market and the train.
11:45 – Lunch in Amphawa.
13:00 – Drive back to Bangkok.
14:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Amphawa evening market and firefly boat trip can replace the morning programme on Friday to Sunday.
• The train schedule at Maeklong changes occasionally; we confirm it the day before.
• Bargaining is normal at the floating market; your guide helps.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, paddle boat, coconut-sugar farm visit, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: purchases at the markets, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Why such an early start?
faq.answer: The floating market is at its liveliest early in the morning, and coach groups arrive from about 9:30.

faq.question: Will we see the train at Maeklong?
faq.answer: We time the visit to the train, which runs several times a day. Occasionally the line closes for maintenance; we tell you in advance if that happens.

faq.question: Is the boat included?
faq.answer: Yes, a paddle boat with a local rower for about an hour. A motorboat can be added to see more canals.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, in Amphawa. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the boats, the fruit and the train. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Boarding the paddle boat needs some agility. The railway market is flat but crowded.

faq.question: Is the floating market touristy?
faq.answer: The main canal is commercial; we use a paddle boat and the quieter side canals to give you a more genuine experience.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops. Bargaining at the market is part of the fun, and buying is entirely up to you.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Thailand but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, a hat, sun cream and comfortable shoes.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: November to February is the coolest. The markets run all year, including in the rainy season.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
